out.rationale: Kenton et al. define debate where a judge LLM answers after viewing two debater LLMs argue opposite answers. Engels et al. say they model their debate setup on Kenton et al. (2024), with the debaters as Houdinis and the judge as the Guard, and report judge (Guard) performance scaling with general intelligence rating while debater (Houdini) performance stays constant on TruthfulQA, with similar behaviour on QuALITY and PrOntoQA, and call this consistent with prior work including Kenton et al.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: debate scaling results from a debate setup that Engels et al. model on Kenton et al.'s

open_obligations: Do not read Engels et al.'s constant debater (Houdini) performance as contradicting Kenton et al.'s debater-strength effect without matching metrics.
Note Engels et al.'s very small question sets.
Check whether both use the same notion of debater strength (aggregate Elo versus general intelligence rating).
out.other_title: Debater strength (Elo) vs judge accuracy and correct-answer advantage in debate
out.rationale: Kenton et al. report stronger debaters (higher Elo) yield higher judge accuracy on extractive tasks with a Gemini Pro 1.5 judge, but are less differentiated on closed tasks. Engels et al. report that on TruthfulQA debater (Houdini) performance stays constant while the judge's (Guard's) performance scales with general intelligence rating, with similar scaling on QuALITY and PrOntoQA and mostly flat performance for both roles on BoolQ; they relate performance to general intelligence rating, whereas Kenton et al. relate judge accuracy to debaters' aggregate Elo.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: how debater and judge capability shape debate outcomes for LLMs
